title: Quantization Pareto Frontier smoke test — jun 2028
content:
Summary:

This doc captures a lightweight exploratory benchmark aimed at mapping a Pareto-style frontier for quantization choices across latency, throughput, memory, and output quality. The goal was not to produce final numbers but to validate an experiment matrix and identify obvious sweet spots and failure modes before a broader, reproducible sweep.

Why this felt useful:
- We keep getting questions from product and SRE about how far we can push aggressive quantization (AWQ, GPTQ, INT8, FP8) without visible quality regressions on customer prompts and long-context workloads.
- Most previous docs (deep sweeps) focus on per-kernel throughput; we wanted a compact cross-axis visualization approach (latency vs quality) to inform a Pareto recommendation for default routing and fallback ordering.

High-level approach and novelty:
- Instead of full-grid, we selected 3 quant families (GPTQ, AWQ, static INT8) + two FP8 variants (E4M3-like and E5M2-like proxies) and 4 kernel implementations (vectorized-tiling, fused-attn, mixed-lane, scalar-fallback).
- For each quant+kernel pair we measured: p50/p95 tail token latency, tokens/sec (sustained on 8xA100 equivalent pool), RTX memory usage for model + KV cache, and "task-quality" via embedding cosine on retrieval QA and log-prob delta on a held-out conversational prompt set.
- Key novelty: we define a simple numeric quality penalty metric (Qpen) that combines embedding cosine drop and normalized log-likelihood delta so we can plot a 2D frontier where x=latency, y=Qpen (lower is better quality).

Workloads:
- Short interactive: 32-token completion prompts (chat style, 1-shot instructions) — captures latency SLOs and tail behavior.
- Long-context: 8k token conditioned summarization workload (single request that grows KV cache activity).
- Retrieval QA batch: 64 parallel queries where we compare embedding similarity (anchor to reference) and exact match on short answers.

Models used (proxies):
- llama-2-13b (open checkpoint used as baseline)
- redwood-tuned-13b-v1 (internal smaller-tuned model to check sensitivity)

Experiment matrix (compact):
- Quant families: GPTQ-4bit, AWQ-4bit, static-INT8 (symmetric), FP8-proxy-lowdynamic, FP8-proxy-highdynamic
- Kernels: fused-attn, vector-tiles, mixed-lane, scalar-fallback
- Runtime knobs: enable-prefix-caching (on/off), batchsize (1 vs 8), KV-reserve (small/large)
- Each cell: 30 warmup runs + 200 measured requests for short workloads; single-run for long-context with microprofiling.

Metrics and Qpen definition:
- p95_token_latency_ms: measured across tokens for streaming responses.
- sustained_tokens_per_sec: measured at stable phase (after 10 tokens) for parallel work.
- memory_resident_mb: model weights + peak KV footprint.
- embedding_cosine_drop: 1 - cosine(quant_embeddings, fp16_embeddings) averaged across retrieval QA set.
- ll_delta: avg(logp_fp16 - logp_quant) normalized by sequence length.
- Qpen = embedding_cosine_drop * 0.6 + sigmoid_clamped(ll_delta)*0.4 (arbitrary weights for exploratory comparison).

Quick results (summary, numeric values are approximate & indicative):
- AWQ-4bit + fused-attn: p95 ~ 22ms (short), sustained 1200 tok/s, memory ~ 23GB, Qpen ~ 0.06 -> strong front-runner for hosted low-cost route.
- GPTQ-4bit + vector-tiles: p95 ~ 18ms, sustained 980 tok/s, memory ~ 20GB, Qpen ~ 0.10 -> slightly faster tail but worse embedding drift on retrieval tasks (some semantic drop).
- static-INT8 + mixed-lane: p95 ~ 28ms, sustained 1100 tok/s, memory ~ 26GB, Qpen ~ 0.04 -> surprisingly robust on logp tasks but larger memory due to less compression efficiency; good for throughput-heavy batch jobs.
- FP8-proxy-lowdynamic + fused-attn: p95 ~ 26ms, sustained 1150 tok/s, memory ~ 21GB, Qpen ~ 0.03 -> best quality but not lowest latency; useful as internal baseline with minimal quality regression.
- FP8-proxy-highdynamic + scalar-fallback: p95 ~ 45ms, sustained 680 tok/s, memory ~ 20GB, Qpen ~ 0.02 -> excellent quality but scalar fallback killed throughput.

Interpretation / patterns:
- There is not a single winner. The Pareto frontier has two limbs: low-latency moderate-quality (AWQ/GPTQ with fused/vector kernels) and high-quality moderate-latency (FP8 proxies with fused kernels).
- Kernel selection matters more than quant family for tail latency. Fused-attn implementations dramatically reduce p95 jitter vs scalar-fallback or mixed-lane under concurrent requests.
- Embedding tasks are more sensitive to GPTQ distortion; AWQ did better for embeddings in our small sample. This suggests routing for embedding endpoints should favor AWQ or FP8 proxies first.
- Memory doesn't always correlate with quality: INT8 sometimes used more memory depending on packing/unpacking strategy in the kernel. Need to standardize measurement (resident vs device-allocated vs temporary workspace).

Operational takeaways (short):
- Default routing recommendation (hosted): prefer AWQ-4bit + fused-attn for interactive chat endpoints where latency is prioritized with tolerable small embedding drift.
- Embedding endpoints: prefer AWQ or FP8-proxy; add a small A/B rollout to monitor embedding downstream metrics (recall/f1).
- Batch inference (high throughput): consider static INT8 + mixed-lane kernels to maximize sustained tok/s, accept slightly higher p95.
- Always have a fallback to FP8-proxy/scalar path for canary failures — graceful degradation path preserves quality at cost of latency.

Open questions & follow-ups:
- The Qpen weighting is ad hoc. We should run user-visible evals (semantic search A/B, downstream retrieval precision) to calibrate the mapping from embedding_cosine_drop/ll_delta to product metrics.
- Kernel instrumentation: need more detailed per-thread stall and memory copy breakdown; current NVPROF samples are coarse. Ticket: GH:repo/bench/issue-412.
- Try linear interpolation between AWQ and GPTQ scales (a toy mixing where keys use AWQ and values use GPTQ) — early experiments seemed promising on some prompts (see appendix commands) but requires formalization.
- Repeat key cells on AMD/ARM devices (we only tested NVIDIA A100-equivalents). Cross-arch playbook item.

Appendix: commands and quick harness notes (notes-to-self):
- harness: bench/smoke_pareto.py --model llama-2-13b --quant AWQ4 --kernel fused-attn --warm 30 --measure 200 --batch 1 --cache on --out csv
- embedding eval: bench/embed_eval.py --ref embeddings/fp16-l2 --quant X --kernel Y --thresholds 0.98,0.95
- long-context profiling: run with --trace api and collect KV hit/miss; watch for stalls at token 2048/4096 boundary.

Known limitations of this doc:
- Small sample sizes and single-region hardware baseline. Not reproducible across teams yet.
- Qpen is exploratory and will bias decisions if used without downstream signal.

Immediate next steps (owners):
- Aditi: spin up a reproducible CI sweep for top 8 pareto cells and add full downstream embedding A/B (JIRA:SRV-1284) — due 2028-06-26.
- Lena: add kernel-level NVTX markers in fused-attn and vector-tiles and re-run p95 stability test — due 2028-06-20.
- Me (Marcus): draft a short PRD with routing recommendations and canary rollout plan for hosted API endpoints (deadline 2028-07-02).

If you want the raw CSV outputs/grafana dashboard links, see linked_artifacts above or ping me in #serving-runtime.

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally compact — flag any cells you think are high value and I will expand them into a reproducible script and timeboxed sweep.
